- Phase A: Staging validation (prefix caching enabled, no rate limiting)
- Phase B: Pilot (10% traffic with 200ms token ceiling + 2s response timeout)
- Phase C: Gradual 100% shift with KV cache warmup and 1% canary rollback window

Hi team —

Quick engineering clarifications from our side (I’m copying the relevant lines into the Drive doc too):

1) Timeouts & retries recommended defaults (client-side):
   - Connect timeout: 250ms
   - Request timeout (per RPC): 2s for small batches, 6s for large sync jobs
   - Retry policy: idempotent-only retries using exponential backoff: 200ms, 400ms, 800ms (max 3 retries)

2) Rate limit headers we emit: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch). We also return 429 with a JSON body that includes "recommended_backoff_ms".

3) Cutover fallback controls: we can flip a canary flag to route 10% -> 100% or revert instantly. During the pilot we will also enable prefix/KV cache warmup so latency stabilizes in the first 10 minutes.

4) For the client cert: we will accept mutual-TLS as long as Keystone’s CA chain is included. If mTLS isn’t ready in time, we’ll fall back to IP allowlist + short-lived Bearer token for the pilot.

Deliverables I’ll post by EOD: a small smoke test script (curl + node snippet) and a sample traffic generator to validate rate-limit headers under load.

Laura Bennett
